frame: glTF / Godot: +Y up, metres; origin at the footprint centre on the ground (cabins: the cabin floor centre); the FRONT faces +Z (the aisle / road / customer side); anchors [x, y, z, yaw_deg] in the piece frame (yaw: a right-handed turn about +Y, Godot's Basis(UP, deg_to_rad(yaw)))
slot_mechanism: a glTF primitive per slot (material mk_<slot>); COLOR_0 = a grey SHADE (baked AO); the runtime multiplies it by the palette colour of the slot (palettes[key][variant][slot], sRGB) into the merged chunk's vertex colour, and merges by GROUP (one draw per group per chunk). Textured groups sample their atlas with UV0 (alpha scissor 0.5, back faces culled: two-faced cards carry their own back).

night.emissive: palette colour x 2.0 HDR x night (bulbs, neon, lamp lenses, obstruction lights)
night.glow: palette colour x 0.9 x night at most (lit faces: lantern glass and paper, lightboxes, cabin ceiling panels)
night.canvas: albedo + albedo x 0.35 x night (tent cloth read through from inside; never over 0.9)
night.tex: emit mask (the atlas _emit.png, L) x albedo x 2.0 x night (letters/neon 255 -> 2.0, faces 115 -> <= 0.9, boards 0)
night.day: emissive and glow groups show their palette colour x 0.85 as albedo

collide.frame: ONLY the boxes in `frame` ([lo, hi], piece frame), never the triangles
collide.ramps: extra walking quads (4 points each, both faces collide), e.g. a station platform's ramps

passes: walk-through volumes [{box: [lo, hi], kind: open|door}] (>= 2.2 m tall, >= 1 m wide; the check proves no triangle or frame box is inside)
walk: [[x0, z0, x1, z1, y]] floor areas people stand on: the check proves >= 2.2 m of head room over them
mid: {glb, mesh, tris}: the MID level (fewer sides, small parts gone) in kit_mid.glb, or kit.glb when the full piece is already cheap

lod1.keep: keep the MID at LOD1 (silhouettes: tents, landmarks, sheds, poles)

fm_pier_deck_6.notes: a 6 x 6 m floating deck module (boards, stringers, two pontoons, fenders); the deck's top at y 0 (the water 0.55 m below), tile it edge to edge

fm_pier_rail_6.notes: 6 m of the pier's edge rail: posts every 2 m, a top rail, a mid rail and a rope

fm_pier_ramp.notes: the shore gangway: 12 m long, 2.6 m wide, 1.0 m from the landing (z -6) down to the deck (z +6); walk it on its `ramps` quad, the side frames are the rails

fm_pier_bollard.notes: a mooring bollard on the deck (the pier head's anchor points: the islands' hawsers make fast here)
